author: HaloGuardian101
body: Hello. In the last few weeks or so, reports on walls haven't been seen, Staff turn off their reports and never come on for team killing, hacking or abusing glitches etc. Team killing is becoming more excessive because when the person reports the mod takes an hour to get there then finally comes and the person is dead. Honestly I think staff are being way to harsh on team killing proof. You need video evidence. You do realise that when you start recording up it takes forever then you are dead.

replies.author: kycrafft
replies.body:
From a staff's perspective, it's really hard to catch teamkilling in walls. Teamkilling usually happens very fast and therefore the reports usually only come after the person has died. 

Addressing the proof issue: There needs to be sufficient evidence to show that the player has indeed teamkilled. Therefore, the two most effective ways to catch at teamkiller are video evidence or a staff witnessing the event. Almost everything else cannot prove the teamkilling without traces of doubt. In the interest of fairness we have to give the person accused of teamkilling the benifit of the doubt if the evidence is not clear. I know this is a problem and I'll personally work on it, but I will let you know that this is tough to deal with.

replies.author: SnowSX3
replies.body:
I think staff are being way to harsh on team killing proof

Video evidence is the only form of sufficient evidence that we can take. Because screenshots can be altered and changed.

Unfortunately, as difficult as it is, it's the only way that the staff team can 100% know exactly what happened.

As for the staff activity, only a few staff turn off their reports and when they do, it's only for a short amount of time.
We take all reports that come in, regardless of what the report says. So I'm not sure where you got this from:

Staff turn off their reports and never come on for team killing, hacking or abusing glitches etc.

replies.author: ID10
replies.body:
Team killing is becoming more excessive because when the person reports the mod takes an hour to get there then finally comes and the person is dead. 

Unfortunately mods can't be on 100% of time to check every report. There is no 'automatic punishing system', it's just a group of people. They could be playing on the server as well, but they are not forced to check into a report as soon as it's sent, but they will eventually (hopefully) deal with it.
